item.title: [9] Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr6Sb6
item.description:
Last authors: Tianping Ying, Mingquan He

Authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important electronic-structure-linked transport study on a kagome material, highly relevant to user interest.

Tags: #kagome #correlated #transport

Abstract: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

item.title: [7] Microscopic origin of field-induced multiferroicity in Ni3TeO6
item.description:
Last authors: A. M. L\"auchli, H. M. R{\o}nnow, K. Lefmann, D. G. Mazzone

Authors: J. Lass, R. Toft-Petersen, A. A. Turrini, {\O}. S. Fjellv{\aa}g, B. Decrausaz, K. M. L. Krighaar, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering study on magnetic topological material with cross-coupling relevance.

Tags: #neutronscattering #magnetism #material

Abstract: The continued demand for smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient technologies has driven condensed-matter research towards materials combining multiple responses within a single phase. Particularly interesting examples are multiferroic materials featuring cross-couplings between order parameters. Ni3TeO6 is a prominent member of this material class, exhibiting a hysteresis-free transition under magnetic field which simultaneously affects the magnetic structure, electric polarization, and phonon frequencies. Here, we uncover the microscopic origin of this multiferroic transition using a combination of neutron scattering techniques. We establish the presence of a finite Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange term giving rise to non-reciprocal, chiral spin waves which soften in magnetic field. Their condensation alters the magnetic structure which controls the electric polarization and drives an ionic displacement, thereby coupling the magnetic, electric, and lattice degrees of freedom. Our study demonstrates that neutron scattering is a powerful technique to elucidate microscopic interactions in multiferroic materials, informing the design of next-generation electronic devices.

item.title: [8] Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
item.description:
Last authors: Nicolas Lorente, Deung-Jang Choi

Authors: Jinkyung Kim, Piotr Kot, Ryo Ogawa, et al.

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: STM/STS study on Majorana zero modes in hybrid superconductor chains; high experimental relevance.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #STS #Majorana #superconductivity

Abstract: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.

item.title: [9] Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Jae Whan Park, Han Woong Yeom

Authors: Abdurrafi Ahsan Alghifari, Euihwan Do, Jae Whan Park, Han Woong Yeom

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of chiral CDW and lattice instabilities in a prototypical quantum material; directly relevant to user interests.

Tags: #CDW #nematic #theory

Abstract: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

item.title: [8] Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
item.description:
Last authors: Jun-ichi Yamaura, Yoshihiko Okamoto

Authors: Keita Nagasawa, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Yoshihiko Okamoto

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Transport study on 112-related telluride; directly aligns with the user's materials interests.

Tags: #material #transport #vanderWaals

Abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. The resulting AMR ratio reaches -33% at 8 K and 10 T and exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence qualitatively captured by a minimal spin-disorder model. These results show that engineering the local environment of dilute magnetic ions provides a route to large paramagnetic AMR without long-range magnetic order, extending the materials design space for AMR beyond magnetically ordered systems.

item.title: [7] Perpendicular Magnetization from Crystallite Boundaries in Polycrystalline Antiferromagnetic -FeMn
item.description:
Last authors: Vsevolod M. Ivanov, Satoru Emori

Authors: Rachel E. Maizel, Sachli Abdizadeh, Ali Almahmoud, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on anomalous Hall effect and magnetic order in polycrystalline antiferromagnets.

Tags: #anomalousHall #antiferromagnet #material

Abstract: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn$_3$Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication. Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic $\gamma$-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, $\gamma$-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites. When the crystallite size $D$ falls below $\approx$ 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density $\propto 1/D$. This magnetization is accompanied by a room-temperature anomalous Hall conductivity exceeding 10 S/cm, comparable to that of single-crystalline Mn$_3$Sn. Our systematic experimental results, including scanning magnetometry, indicate uncompensated spin moments in the boundaries coupled to the compensated antiferromagnetism within the crystallites. We further find that the perpendicular easy axis of the magnetization is stabilized by residual strain within the $\gamma$-FeMn film. Our findings in manufacturing-friendly polycrystalline $\gamma$-FeMn redefine crystal defects as enablers, rather than impediments, for scalable antiferromagnetic memory.

item.title: [7] Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La2O2Fe2OSe2 by broad range 139La-NQR
item.description:
Last authors: Bernd B"uchner, Hans-Henning Klauss

Authors: Tillmann Weinhold, Jerin Abraham George, Cornelius Herrmann, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: NMR/NQR investigation of magnetic order in a complex iron-based material.

Tags: #magnetism #material

Abstract: The transition metal oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ exhibits a non-collinear spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx $ 90 K due to complex magnetic exchange interactions and axial single-ion anisotropy of Fe$^{2+}$ spins. The magnetic structure was deduced/determined from combined $^{57}$Fe M"ossbauer spectroscopy and $^{139}$La-NMR on polycrystalline specimen. In this work, we present zero-field $^{139}$La-NQR investigations on polycrystalline La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ in a broad frequency and temperature range between 2.8 - 20 MHz and 4.2 - 100 K. The measured resonances at ${ u}_Q$, $2 \, { u}_Q$, and $3 \, { u}_Q$ are fully consistent with the previous NMR studies and also with the magnetic structure. A substantial modification of the electric field gradient at the La-position below $T_N$ is inconsistent with the current investigations.

item.title: [8] Effect of Annealing on Maze Domains in Topological Insulator - Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Sean Langridge, Christopher H. Marrows

Authors: Benjamin A. Brereton, Soumyarup Hait, Christy J. Kinane, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on topological insulator/magnetic heterostructures using photoemission-related technique.

Tags: #topologicalinsulator #heterostructure #magnetism #photoemission

Abstract: Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

item.title: [9] Spin order and excitations in the collinear kagome antiferromagnet Y0.5Fe3Sn3 (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Enke Liu, Huiqian Luo

Authors: Jin Ding, Yang Liu, Feihao Pan, et al.

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Experimental neutron scattering and AHE study on a kagome antiferromagnet, very relevant to user.

Tags: #kagome #neutronscattering #anomalousHall #antiferromagnet #transport

Abstract: Kagome lattices host rich magnetic, topological, and transport phenomena owing to their geometric frustration and strong spin correlations. Here we present a systematic neutron scattering study of the kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$, which orders into a collinear $c$-axis antiferromagnetic (AF) state below $T_N =$ 551 K. An additional anomalous Hall effect (AHE) contribution beyond the conventional magnetization-scaling response is observed well below $T_N$ under an in-plane magnetic field $\mathbf{B} \parallel ab$. Elastic neutron scattering demonstrates that the Fe moments preserve their collinear $c$-axis AF alignment down to 1.5 K at zero field. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals a distinctive Y-shape spin excitation dispersion exhibiting a two-gap structure below 10 meV, likely arising from two nondegenerate spin-wave branches. Polarized neutron measurements further show that the low-temperature spin excitations are strongly anisotropic: the in-plane component $M_{ab}$ dominates while the $c$-axis component $M_c$ is nearly absent. Upon warming, $M_c$ gradually grows markedly but remains much weaker than $M_{ab}$ even at 300 K. We propose that the unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting either in the static or dynamic configurations due to gapless excitations. These findings establish the collinear AF kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$ as a platform for chirality-driven AHE without spontaneous spin reorientation.

item.title: [7] Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe2Mo3O8
item.description:
Last authors: Hong-Hao Song, Gang v. Chen

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory for real material system (honeycomb molybdate) discussing Berry curvature and Hall effect.

Tags: #theory #magnetism #Berrycurvature #Halleffect #realmaterials

Abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

Abstract: The iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of non-layered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, the issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe-Ge system. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ~4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation (SHG) signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centro-symmetry of the cubic phase. SQUID magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin-orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

Abstract: The interaction of quantum systems with ultrashort laser pulses may lead to transient states far from equilibrium. Abstract: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. Abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moir\'e systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. Abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

item.title: [8] Comment on "InAs-Al hybrid devices passing the topological gap protocol", Microsoft Quantum, Phys. Rev. B 107, 245423 (2023)
item.description:
Last authors: Henry F. Legg

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Critical discussion of Majorana signatures and experimental protocols in semiconductor-superconductor hybrid devices.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #experiment #Majorana #topological-superconductivity

Abstract: The topological gap protocol (TGP) is presented as "a series of stringent experimental tests" for the presence of topological superconductivity and associated Majorana zero modes. Here, we show that the TGP, "passed" by Microsoft Quantum [PRB 107, 245423 (2023)], lacks a consistent definition of "gap" or "topological", and even utilises different code when applied to theoretical simulations compared to experimental data. Furthermore, the outcome of the TGP is sensitive to the choice of magnetic field range, bias voltage range, data resolution, and cutter voltage pair (junction transparency) -- data parameters that, in PRB 107, 245423 (2023), vary significantly, even for measurements of the same device. As a result, the core claims of PRB 107, 245423 (2023) are based on unexplained measurement choices and inconsistent definitions. In particular, this means the claim by Microsoft Quantum in PRB 107, 245423 (2023) that their devices have a "high probability of being in the topological phase" is not reliable and should be revisited. In light of this, subsequent studies that are based on tuning up devices via the TGP should also be revisited.

item.description:
Last authors: Jing-Yu Zhao, Ya-Hui Zhang

Published as: Nat. Commun. DOI

Abstract: Understanding the mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is a central challenge in correlated moir\'e materials. The most intriguing question is about the nature of the normal state: is the Cooper pair formed from small Fermi surface or large Fermi surface? item.title: [9] Pseudogap and Non-Fermi-liquid criticality in double Kondo model for bilayer nickelates
item.description:
Last authors: Jing-Yu Zhao, Ya-Hui Zhang

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure and pseudogap physics of bilayer nickelates using DMFT.

Tags: #theory #nickelates #correlated-electrons #DMFT

Abstract: Motivated by recent experimental progress on high-temperature superconductivity in bilayer nickelates, we investigate the phase diagram of the normal state in a bilayer Kondo lattice model using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). When the interlayer tunneling $t_\perp$ is absent, we identify a non-Fermi-liquid (NFL) critical point tuned by the interlayer spin coupling $J_\perp$ or hole doping $x$, which separates a standard Fermi liquid in the overdoped region from a distinct pseudogap (PG) metal in the underdoped regime. This PG phase, which we term the `second Fermi liquid' (sFL), exhibits small hole pockets and violates the perturbative Luttinger theorem despite the absence of symmetry breaking or fractionalization. The PG metal behaves like a heavy Fermi liquid, with small quasi-particle residue and large effective mass. We also provide an intuitive analytical description of the pseudogap and the ground-state wave function based on an ancilla-fermion framework. Inside the PG phase, we interpret the ancilla fermion as a spin-polaron and demonstrate a Kondo-like resonance peak in the spectral function of this composite fermion directly in DMFT calculation. Extending the analysis to finite $t_\perp$, we apply this framework to the bilayer nickelate $\mathrm{La}_3\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_7$. We propose that current experimental samples ($x \approx 0.5$) reside in the overdoped FL regime, suggesting that the pseudogap phase and the NFL criticality may be accessed via electron doping.

item.title: [8] Robust Signatures of Fragile Topology in Nonmagnetic Materials
item.description:
Last authors: Jasper van Wezel, Cosma Fulga

Authors: Viktor K\"onye, Ihor Nimyi, Oleg Janson, Jeroen van den Brink, Jasper van Wezel, Cosma Fulga

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Identifies Dirac points in nonmagnetic materials using fragile topology indices with direct spectroscopic relevance.

Tags: #theory #topology #Diracpoints #bandstructure

Abstract: Some topological phases of matter are called fragile. They can be trivialized by adding additional valence bands and do not generically host protected gapless boundary states. Here we establish a fragile topological index with a bulk signature: it guarantees the presence of gap closing points in the bulk band structure of systems with both time-reversal and twofold rotation symmetry. This result extends the established use of the Euler class in diagnosing the presence of Dirac cones for general two-dimensional systems with a combination of time-reversal and twofold rotation symmetry, to the case of nonmagnetic materials obeying both symmetries individually. The abundance of natural nonmagnetic materials with these symmetries renders the topological invariant practically useful, despite its fragility. We demonstrate this by applying first-principles calculations to five materials and finding that all of them host Dirac points identified by the invariant, suggesting its widespread applicability. Our results thus provide a robust spectroscopic signature of fragile topology in nonmagnetic systems which can be directly accessed in experiments on practically relevant materials. Furthermore, they enable an alternate method for finding Dirac cones in ab-initio simulations, and may be used as a route towards identifying materials with nonlinear transport properties.

item.title: [10] Drumhead Surface States of Rhombohedral Graphite with Near Ideal Quantum Geometry Condition
item.description:
Last authors: Lin-Lin Wang

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct spectroscopic study of drumhead surface states in graphite with ARPES comparison and flat-band topology.

Tags: #photoemission #ARPES #graphene #topology #flatbands

Abstract: The ideal quantum geometry (IQG) condition for the trace of quantum metric ($TrG(k)$) being equal to the magnitude of Berry curvature (|$\Omega(k)$|) as in $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$=1 has been associated with realizing fractional Chern insulators for the flat bands in a few layers of rhombohedral graphene (RG). More recently the IQG condition has also been proposed for superconductivity in the flat bands of thick RG layers. Using density functional theory and Wannier functions, we study the symmetry-protected topology of bulk RG, drumhead surface states (DSS) of semi-infinite RG surface and slabs, and the IQG condition for thin and thick RG slabs. We find that bulk RG is a weak topological insulator with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), besides being effectively a chiral semimetal with chiral nodal lines without SOC. We also find that the DSS flat bands of thick RG slabs have a sizable convex curvature with dispersion depth agreeing with the recent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy experiment. The calculated IQG also shows a convex shape with the K point at the center having a minimum with approximately $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$$\approx$1. But the inner rim of the DSS region approaches the IQG condition of $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$=1. These results on thick RG slabs from first-principles calculations provide useful information for the pristine DSS at the single-particle level for future studies to consider when enhanced electron correlation and many-body interaction will be included.

item.description:
Last authors: Si Li, Wen-Li Yang

Authors: Jin-Yang Li, Ruo-Yu Ning, Ying Zhang, Qiu-Qiu Li, Si Li, Wen-Li Yang

Why: Floquet-engineered spin splitting and altermagnetism in CoS/CoSe with anomalous Hall response.

Tags: #theory #Floquet #altermagnetism #anomalousHall #antiferromagnet

Abstract: Altermagnetism, characterized by compensated collinear magnetic moments and even-parity momentum-dependent spin splitting, has emerged as a distinct form of magnetic order. However, realizing odd- and mixed-parity magnetism in fully compensated collinear magnets remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate light-induced odd- and mixed-parity magnetism in conventional collinear antiferromagnets. Combining Floquet theory with first-principles calculations, we show that circularly polarized light (CPL) induces odd-parity $f$-wave spin splitting in monolayer CoS and CoSe, whereas elliptically polarized light (EPL) induces $p$-wave spin splitting. Uniaxial strain combined with CPL offers an alternative route to the $p$-wave state. Furthermore, combining an electric field with CPL or EPL generates mixed-parity spin splitting. Light-induced breaking of $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, together with spin-orbit coupling, gives rise to a finite anomalous Hall response. Our findings establish a versatile approach to engineering spin splitting and controlling electronic and magnetic properties in compensated antiferromagnets.

item.description:
Last authors: Jyotirmoy Sau

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on Berry curvature dipole and nonlinear Hall effect in a relevant honeycomb model.

Tags: #theory #transport #Berrycurvature #machinelearning

Abstract: A Berry-curvature dipole can produce a nonlinear Hall current even when the linear Hall response vanishes, but symmetry alone does not determine its magnitude or magnetic tunability. The interplay of structural symmetry, moment orientation, and carrier occupation is examined in a honeycomb model. Curvature maps and the band-summed dipole integrand reveal how velocity and the occupation window near the Fermi level select signed contributions. Removing threefold rotation permits a nonmagnetic dipole perpendicular to the surviving mirror. Generic magnetic reorientation activates the second component and tunes both components through positive and negative values. Global reversal preserves the dipole while reversing the intrinsic linear Hall conductivity, allowing a finite bulk dipole contribution from equally populated reversed domains under uniform-field averaging.A symmetry-constrained polynomial model predicts both dipole components for 256 held-out spin configurations, achieving coefficients of determination $R^2 > 0.9995$ at the reference chemical potential. At fixed carrier density, orientation-dependent shifts of the chemical potential modify the response and yield slightly larger prediction errors for the chosen model. Across the chemical-potential sweep,the prediction accuracy decreases more strongly for $D_y$,revealing an energy dependence of the surrogate's performance. Within semiclassical transport with a constant relaxation time, the calculated dipole determines the angular dependence of the quadratic current and its rectified and second-harmonic components. These results provide a quantitative representation of magnetic-orientation-dependent Berry-curvature dipoles and show how carrier occupation influences both the response and its predictability.

item.description:
Last authors: Jack Gartside, Mathieu Mivelle

Authors: Xingyu Yang, Tristan da C\^amara Santa Clara Gomes, Chantal Hareau, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental control of magnetic skyrmions, relevant to magnetic topological materials.

Tags: #magnetism #skyrmions #opto-magnetism #metasurfaces

Abstract: Magnetic skyrmions hold high promise for low power spintronic and neuromorphic computing. However, existing manipulation schemes rely predominantly on local thermal excitation, rendering nucleation stochastic and lacking a non-destructive mechanism for targeted erasure. Here, we demonstrate a deterministic, optomagnetic field-driven paradigm for fast, all-optical writing and erasing of magnetic skyrmion crystals using a magneto-plasmonic metasurface. By tailoring surface lattice resonances in a periodic nanodisk array, circularly polarized light excites giant super-circular optical spin densities that drive intense circulating drift photocurrents via the inverse Faraday effect. This delivers synchronized picosecond magnetic field pulses into an adjacent magnetic multilayer. Micromagnetic simulations reveal that a single optical pulse deterministically nucleates stable N\'eel skyrmions through a transient Bloch to N\'eel relaxation pathway governed by optical helicity and interfacial Dzyaloshinskii Moriya interaction. Crucially, reversing incident light helicity allows on-demand topological reconfiguration: under a confining bias field, the inverted optomagnetic field unwinds pre existing skyrmions to restore a uniform ground state. Furthermore, we demonstrate the targeted writing of stable skyrmionium states. By bypassing stochastic thermal cycles and achieving reversible topological control on picosecond timescales, this work bridges nanophotonics, plasmonics, and magnetism, establishing a scalable foundation for high-speed, reconfigurable information processing and unconventional computing.

By bypassing stochastic thermal cycles and achieving reversible topological control on picosecond timescales, this work bridges nanophotonics, plasmonics, and magnetism, establishing a scalable foundation for high-speed, reconfigurable information processing and unconventional computing.
